card.problem: The orchestrator is the last context that lives as long as the whole fleet. It can end and be re-dispatched, resuming from run.yaml. The question is at which boundary it is allowed to end.
useCases: a 7-unit fleet across 3 waves on one laptop
a wave whose lane ends gate-red in /build having pushed nothing

options.label: Wave completion only

walks.text: the orchestrator ends 3 times; each tick holds one wave's dispatches, notifications and reconciliation
the wave is still complete (every lane reported), so the tick ends; that unit's commits live only in its worktree, which survives because teardown needs terminal: true
breaks — unpushed lane commits are local-only

options.rejectedBecause: the same boundary with the safety half dropped: it leaves a gate-red lane commits only in its worktree, so the run cannot move machines and a recycled worktree loses them

options.label: Wave completion, and push every started branch first

walks.text: identical to A, plus one push per started lane at the boundary
its commits reach origin, so the next tick can resume from any tree
survives — this is the existing cost-stop protocol, generalised to every yield

options.label: Any time, with lanes as detached claude -p processes

walks.text: the orchestrator ends whenever it likes; lanes write verdicts on their branches via lane-step-record
the verdict is on the branch, readable by any later tick
survives, but needs process management the plugin has never done and drops the Agent tool's notification path

options.rejectedBecause: premise unverified: whether a claude -p exit kills its background subagents is a known-unknown; take it only if B's per-wave context still measures too large

recommendation.why: /start-multi already defines a cost stop at exactly this boundary and already says what it costs to stop there: 'git push every started lane's branch first and keep its worktree, because a lane that has not reached /verify-build has pushed nothing.' A is that stop with the safety half dropped.

card.ifOverturned: C makes the driver a process supervisor and the tracer bullet becomes the subagent-lifetime probe instead of a two-unit fleet

forks.title: Who re-dispatches the orchestrator, and what stops a driver looping forever

card.problem: Something must re-invoke /start-multi after each yield. /build's yield already has this exact loop one level down, and it ships with a non-progress guard: 'k did not advance between two consecutive dispatches -> stop and report blocked-on=build-no-progress; a yield that resumes onto the same slice forever is the one way this loop costs more than it saves.' Whatever drives the orchestrator needs the same guard.
useCases: a wave that yields without advancing because its lane keeps dying

walks.text: one fresh claude -p per tick until the verdict is terminal; no context survives between ticks
the driver owns the guard: compare waves=k/N across two ticks and stop on no progress, mirroring build-no-progress
a bin/ script with a scripts/ implementation and a test-*.sh; the agent census stays 11, and the bin/ name is a contract from the day it ships

options.label: The human re-invokes each tick

walks.text: does not run overnight; unattended is /start-multi's stated contract
the human sees it, so no mechanical guard is needed
nothing new ships

options.rejectedBecause: breaks the unattended contract the command states in its first line

options.label: /loop inside one session

walks.text: runs, but the babysitter's own context is the 403k-median row; it re-loads the orchestration bodies into a context that never ends
the babysitter would have to hold the guard in prose, in the context we are trying to end
nothing new ships

options.rejectedBecause: it re-creates the unbounded context this work exists to remove

recommendation.why: it is the only option that keeps the unattended contract while ending the context, and the guard it must carry is already specified and proven one level down in unit-lane's /build loop

card.ifOverturned: B drops the driver slice entirely and the work is only the yield plus the resume point

forks.title: How a yield is spelled in the verdict line

card.problem: The issue proposed a new marker carrying outcome=yield. The evidence says that word has nowhere to land. remote-ai-agents' verdict.ts hardcodes exactly three outcomes (success, gate-red, blocked-on) and maps anything else to infra with infraReason 'unknown-outcome'; unit-lane's spec block emits the same three. /build already expresses a yield without a fourth word: 'a yield is a success whose slices= is short of its total.' Separately, lane-step-parse.py enforces no enum at all but does hardcode the marker token LANE-STEP:v(\d+).
useCases: the driver reads the tick's verdict to decide whether to tick again
remote-ai-agents leases a step and reads the same line

options.label: New marker FLEET-STEP:v1, with outcome=yield

walks.text: works — the driver is new code and can know the word
unknown-outcome -> infra, if the line ever reaches that reader
two yield vocabularies in one flow: success-with-short-counts at the slice level, outcome=yield at the wave level

options.rejectedBecause: invents a fourth outcome word for a concept the flow already spells a different way one level down

options.label: New marker FLEET-STEP:v1, reusing the three outcomes; a yield is success with waves=k/N short of total

walks.text: success with k<N means tick again, exactly as unit-lane reads slices=3/8
the outcome vocabulary is the one it already knows; only the marker token differs
one yield idiom at both levels; lane-step-parse needs its marker parameterised and nothing else, since its attribute grammar already accepts waves=k/N

options.label: Reuse LANE-STEP:v1 with step=start-multi

walks.text: works with today's parser unchanged
verdict.ts compares step against the step the scheduler leased, so an unleased step is wrong-step -> infra; it holds no enum, so this is about the lease, not a list
one marker for two different things: a pipeline step and a fleet tick

options.rejectedBecause: conflates a step's verdict with a run's; the orchestrator is not one of the five leased steps

recommendation.why: it is the only option that adds a marker without adding a vocabulary. The correction that drives it: the blocker on C is verdict.ts's expectedStep lease, not a step= enum, and the blocker on A is the three-value OUTCOMES table, which the issue attributed to the wrong place.

card.ifOverturned: A costs a fourth outcome in every reader that ever sees the line; C costs no code today and a conflated contract later

forks.title: Is the resume point stored, or derived from the units

card.problem: The issue proposes three additive run.yaml keys: waveBudget, wavesDone and phase. But /start-multi already carries units[].wave plus step and status, and /design-multi already carries units[].step as pending|drafting|critiqued|resolved|written|done, which is the phase. And the command itself states the principle: 'Git is the primary signal and the state file a hint', naming 'a state file that says step: plan while the branch carries three slices' as the orchestrator's commonest misread. A stored resume pointer is exactly that kind of second truth.
useCases: a tick is killed between dispatch and collection
a lane advances after the orchestrator wrote run.yaml

options.label: Store all three: waveBudget, wavesDone, phase

walks.text: wavesDone says the wave finished; the units say otherwise; the stored value wins and a wave is skipped
the pointer is stale in the dangerous direction
one line to read

options.rejectedBecause: denormalises state the units already determine, in a file the command already calls a hint

options.label: Store only waveBudget; derive wave progress and phase from units[]

walks.text: the next tick derives progress from units[] and git, and re-enters the incomplete wave, which is step 4's existing resume rule
nothing to go stale; the derivation reads the current units
one derivation, which is the same one step 4 already performs

options.label: Store all three, but treat them as hints re-derived on read

walks.text: safe, because the derivation runs anyway
safe, same reason
the stored value is now decoration that must be kept honest by every writer, for no read that trusts it

options.rejectedBecause: pays the write cost of a cache nothing is allowed to read

recommendation.why: waveBudget is a policy input and genuinely not derivable, so it is stored; wavesDone and phase are projections of units[], and the repo has already named the failure mode of storing them.

card.ifOverturned: A makes the invariant 'run.yaml changes are additive' true in letter and adds the misread the command warns about

card.problem: Phase A (unattended lanes) ends with subject maps on disk; Phase B is the one attended sitting; Phase C is the write-back. The issue proposes ending at both A/B and B/C. But Phase B holds a live Monitor websocket and a published design-map page, and Phase C must re-verify the pinned base.
useCases: the owner answers half the forks, then stops for the day

options.label: End at A/B and B/C; the human opens Phase B by hand

walks.text: three sessions; Phase B starts cold on the subject maps, which are its primary source
the answers are in the artifact db, not the session; a fresh Phase B reads them back with read_db
Phase C already re-verifies the pin, so a fresh session changes nothing

options.label: End at A/B only; B and C stay one session

walks.text: two sessions; the largest single context is the sitting plus the whole write-back
same as A, the db holds the answers
unchanged

options.rejectedBecause: Phase C is tracker-writer waves, which is the part that most resembles a wave loop and least needs the sitting's context

options.label: The driver opens Phase B too

walks.text: the driver opens a session nobody is sitting in
no one is there to ask the next question
unchanged

options.rejectedBecause: a driver cannot sit in for the human, and design-multi already batches every human moment into this one phase

recommendation.why: each phase's primary source is already on disk (units/, subjects/, answers/), which is the test for whether ending loses anything; and the sitting is attended by definition, so the human opening it is not a cost.

card.ifOverturned: B drops the phase: resume point to a single A/B boundary and makes slice 2 smaller
